crash-plan.title: How people make millions from a financial collapse: my 5-step crash plan
crash-plan.reel_caption:
How do people make millions from a financial collapse? 💰

They didn't predict the date. They were ready before it hit. My 5-step crash plan:

1️⃣ Weak local currency → fully backed digital dollars, in your own offline wallet (issuers can still freeze, know the risk)
2️⃣ Keep cash ready to buy the panic
3️⃣ Own what people buy in any crisis (staples rose 24% in the dot-com crash)
4️⃣ Watch the companies AI can't run without, but only when cheap (chips −12% in a day on 5 Nov)
5️⃣ Crypto: small slice, long term (billion-dollar families keep ~1%)

People who sold in 2008 were up 2% three years later. People who stayed were up 50%.

crash-plan.li_text:
People who sold their stocks in the 2008 crash were up 2% three years later. People who stayed invested were up 50% (Fidelity, 7.1M accounts).

The ones who made millions, like Ackman in 2020 ($27M of protection → $2.6B) and Buffett in 2008, didn't predict the date. They were ready before it hit.

My 5-step crash plan:
1. Weak local currency → fully backed digital dollars, held in your own wallet, not on an exchange. (Know the risk: issuers can freeze.)
2. Keep cash ready to buy the panic.
3. Own what people buy in any crisis. Consumer staples rose 24% in the dot-com crash while the market halved.
4. Watch the companies AI can't run without: power, chips, robots. Only when cheap; chips fell 12% in a day on 5 Nov.
5. Crypto: a small, long-term slice. Even billion-dollar family offices keep it around 1%.

A crash-tested framework (25% each in stocks, bonds, gold and cash) fell about 3% at the 2009 low while stocks fell half.

My opinion, not financial advice. Everyone decides for themselves.

Which step are you missing?

ex11.title: AI hallucination explained: why ChatGPT invents facts
ex11.reel_caption:
AI hallucination explained: ChatGPT can sound sure and still be completely wrong. ⚖️

In 2023 (Mata v. Avianca), New York lawyers filed court cases ChatGPT gave them. The cases didn't exist, and the judge fined them $5,000. Before you trust an answer: check facts, names, numbers, laws and medical advice in a real source. Ask for sources, then open them yourself.
